title: The Gaussian free field limit of the balanced six-vertex model with variance multiplier 1/arcsin(c/2)
main_claim: For a=b=1 and every 0<c<=2, the iterated balanced-torus plane law P_c exists, and the rescaled height function h_delta converges to sigma(c)*GFF with sigma(c)^2 = 2/arccos(1-c^2/2) = 1/arcsin(c/2). The convergence holds for finite-energy measure tests, in negative Besov/Sobolev/Holder restriction spaces, and for moments of separated increments.

issues.location: Sec. 4 (Lemma inner-spectra, Lemma low-band) and Sec. 5 (Lemma infrared, trace comparison in sec:finite-trace), sections/04-angular-plane.tex and 05-normalization.tex
issues.description: Several key analytic steps are given as compressed sketches rather than complete proofs: the reduction of almost every spectral function to a finite Blaschke product, the claim that the fixed-u susceptibility measure has no atom at phase zero, and the claim that the O_N(d^N) interior error control beats the polynomial P(1/d) losses in the Taylor-trace comparison. I found no step that fails, but a referee would ask for these to be written out in full.
issues.evidence: 'Choosing a higher initial accuracy order therefore makes the interior row errors ... O_N(d^N) ... Their global row bounds have only polynomial costs in 1/d.'

issues.description: At c=2 the plane law is identified with the theorem's balanced iterated torus limit through the paragraph after DKLM Theorem 2.2 ('balanced cylinders'). The paper does not spell out that this is the same order of limits (M to infinity first, then L) as the one in its own definition of P_c.
issues.evidence: 'That paragraph identifies the unrestricted torus limit with the slope-zero law defined through balanced cylinders.'

coverage: Read in full: the introduction and theorem statement, the main proof (Sec. 8), and the normalization section (Sec. 5: Kohn stiffness, infrared lower bound, staggered overlap upper bound, window packing, trace comparison, symbol evaluation). Also read the kernel definitions in Sec. 2, the angular-space construction and the inner-spectra and low-band lemmas in Sec. 4, the c>=1 equilibrium identification in Sec. 4, and the start of the c=2 endpoint appendix. Checks made: (1) the multiplier identity 2/arccos(Delta) = 1/arcsin(c/2). (2) The kernel transforms, 1+K^(0) = 2(pi-lambda)/pi, and r(u) = 1/(2 lambda cosh(u/eta)) with integral 1/2. (3) The stiffness arithmetic 2 * 2pi * (pi/(2(pi-lambda))) / pi^2 = 2/(pi-lambda). (4) The Toeplitz symbol (1-b0)(1+e^{2 pi i z} a0)/(1-a0 b0), checked numerically with mpmath for both signs of p; it agrees to about 1e-16. (5) The quadratic log coefficient -4 pi^2 z^2 a0/(1+a0)^2, its integral 1/(2 pi lambda), and the total -1/(2 lambda(pi-lambda)). (6) The match between the upper and lower bounds on kappa through eta = lambda/pi, and the rapidity-to-log-angle conversion s = x/eta, which is consistent with the B/eta packing length. (7) The external citation: I fetched DKLM2026 (arXiv 2603.06268) and confirmed that Theorem 4.3 (GFF-LDP correspondence) and Theorem 4.4 (f''(0) = -arcsin(c/2)) are stated for c in [1,2]. So their use on 1<=c<sqrt3 is within hypotheses, even though DKLM's headline result only covers c in [sqrt3,2]. The equilibrium characterization after DKLM eq. (6) is also stated for c in [1,2]. Not checked line by line: the thermodynamic estimates in Sec. 3 (root tails, Gaudin inverses, residue conditions), the chiral Wick rules in Sec. 6, the probabilistic endgame in Sec. 7, and most of the FK loop coupling in the appendix.
